newsitem.title: USA: Muni yields rise 10 basis points over past week.
newsitem.headline: Muni yields rise 10 basis points over past week.

text.p: Average yields on investment-grade municipal bonds rose 10 basis points in the week ended Thursday, Delphis Hanover Corp said Friday.
Thirty-year, Aaa-rated municipal yields rose 10 basis points to 5.65 percent, while thirty-year Baa yields were five basis points higher, moving to 6.45 percent.
Despite the yield increases, munis outperformed Treasuries over the week. The Treasury long bond rose 15 basis points during the period, ending Thursday at 6.74 percent.
Thirty-year, Aaa-rated munis were yielding 83.8 percent of the Treasury long bond at the close Thursday.
Average yields on one-year Aaa-rated municipal bonds were up 10 basis points to 3.65 percent, while Baa-rated one-years were yielding 4.50 percent on average.
In the intermediate sector, ten-year Aaa-rated municipal bonds were up 10 basis points to 4.90 percent. Baa-rated ten-years yielded 5.75 percent.
The triple-A yield curve between one-year and 30-year munis was unchanged at 200 basis points. The Baa curve was 195 basis points.
The credit spread between Aaa-rated and Baa-rated one-years was 85 basis points, while the 30-year spread narrowed five basis points to 80 basis points.
